name: Tobiah (the Ammonite)
title: Opponent of Jerusalem's Reconstruction
summary: Tobiah was an Ammonite official who, together with Sanballat, actively opposed Nehemiah's work to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. He used threats, mockery, and political intrigue to hinder the Jews' restoration efforts and had close ties to certain Jewish families through marriage.

keyEvents.title: Mocked the Jews' Wall Building
keyEvents.description: Tobiah ridiculed the Jews' building efforts, saying that even a fox could tear down the stone wall they were constructing.

keyEvents.title: Conspired Against Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: Tobiah collaborated with Sanballat and Geshem to lure Nehemiah into a trap by inviting him to a meeting on the plain of Ono.

keyEvents.title: Sent Threatening Letters
keyEvents.description: Tobiah sent letters to intimidate Nehemiah and weaken his resolve in the rebuilding work.

keyEvents.title: Had connections to Jewish leaders
keyEvents.description: Many in Judah were bound to Tobiah by oath because he was the son-in-law of Shebaniah and his son was married to a Jewish woman.

keyEvents.title: Given space in the temple
keyEvents.description: The priest Eliashib gave Tobiah a large room in the temple courts, which was a great violation of the sanctuary.

keyEvents.title: Cast out of the temple
keyEvents.description: When Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem, he threw all of Tobiah's belongings out of the temple room and cleansed it.
